Chapter 05 of 19

The Probes

Port / Burrard Inlet
The story

Down at the port, the giant cranes stand along the water. To most people they are machinery. In Terminal City they are the Probes, and they are sensory instruments: the city's way of reaching outside itself.

Ships leave with questions. They come back with weather, objects, languages, sounds, rumours, materials and patterns nobody here has seen before. Sometimes the cargo is only the box the information travelled in. The cranes lift it out and pass it on: to the Far Shore for translation, into the Wire Choir as sound, or to the Repair People as a kind of mark the city has never painted.

Without the Probes, Terminal City would only ever feed on itself. And if you see a crane turned to face inland instead of the sea, it has learned something. Send out. Bring back. Lift the signal. What did you see?

Terminal City is an original fictional mythology inspired by Vancouver’s geography, weather, wildlife, infrastructure, art, and electronic music. It makes no claim to historical, Indigenous, or religious tradition. Real places are used as settings; the operating system layered on them is invented. Photograph reality. Alter the evidence. Never illustrate the whole myth.
